correctness.rationale: (1) Orthogonality gives the exact quartic energy. (2) Completing the dyadic valuation split proves \(M(d)=2^{r+2}\) for \(r<k\) and \(2^k\) for \(r\ge k\), including zero. (3) A two-daughter energy estimate has equality precisely at a single parent coset with equal daughter masses. (4) Equality in the Cauchy term for h=\(2^k\), with \(K_h=2^{k-1}R\), forces one cyclic character shared by both daughters; no other supports or phases satisfy equality. (5) Every proposed packet makes all inequalities tight. Reproducible corroboration: checker.py for \(2^{2k}\) of sizes 4,16,64,256; finite checks do not substitute for all-order proof.

value.rationale: A complete optimizer set for a natural sharp Fourier restriction inequality resolves an explicit missing equality classification rather than recomputing the constant. Uniformly for every even dyadic exponent it identifies exact support concentration, phase rigidity within both daughters, freedom between daughters, and the number of projective circle components. Such rigidity matters to optimal sampling and future quantitative stability studies.
